standard.title: Analyse and enhance performance
standard.description: analyse, adapt and refine their own and others' movement skills in a range of challenging movement situations to enhance performance
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can demonstrate and explain how movement concepts can be manipulated to improve movement outcomes (AC9HP8M03). At Y9-10 the focus moves to analysis of performance with feedback — using knowledge of results, digital tools, and constructive peer feedback to refine skills in challenging situations.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse, adapt and refine their own and others' movement skills in challenging situations, using feedback mechanisms including digital tools to enhance performance.

nodes.label: Analysing movement performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse movement performance — their own and others' — identifying what needs to be refined and why
nodes.minimum_width: Observe a movement performance (their own or a peer's) and identify at least two specific aspects that affect the outcome — explain why each matters for performance quality
nodes.typical_width: Use knowledge of results feedback to analyse performance with accuracy and control; analyse performances (e.g. swimming, athletics, cross-country) and propose strategies for refining technique; use digital tools to record and analyse timing of movements in relation to teammates, opposition or external stimuli
wider: Use video analysis tools to compare own performance against a reference model — identify specific timing, positioning or technique differences and explain their effect on outcome
Analyse performance changes when equipment is varied (e.g. different bat weight, ball type, resistance) — evaluate which equipment adaptations improve performance and why

Provide constructive performance feedback to a peer using a structured framework (e.g. two specific observations, one improvement focus) — evaluate whether the feedback resulted in a measurable change
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot analyse what specifically needs to change in a performance cannot meaningfully adapt or refine it in Node 2 — adaptation and refinement require a prior analytical judgement about what the current performance is producing and what it needs to produce instead.

response_modes.reason: Students commonly observe performances and describe what they see without analysing why it matters for performance outcome. The structured reasoning investment is in building the analysis chain: what is the specific movement pattern, what effect does it have on the outcome, what would a refined version look like. Digital tools support this — video allows repeated review that verbal observation cannot match.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two specific aspects of a performance that affect the outcome
Explains why each aspect matters — not just that it is 'good' or 'bad'
Analysis is specific enough to inform a refinement action — generic ('needs to be faster') is insufficient

nodes.label: Adapting and refining skills
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adapt and refine movement skills in response to analysis and feedback across challenging movement situations
nodes.minimum_width: Make one specific adaptation to a movement skill based on analysis; evaluate whether the adaptation improved the performance outcome
nodes.typical_width: Adapt and respond to changes in equipment or conditions that increase complexity; provide and act on constructive feedback on group performance of a movement sequence; analyse performances across multiple activity types and refine techniques in response; evaluate effectiveness of adaptations
wider: Refine performance in response to digital feedback across multiple trial repetitions — evaluate which adaptations produced the most significant improvement and why
Adapt movement skills to a novel activity context (e.g. transfer batting technique to a new sport) and evaluate what transferred effectively and what needed further adaptation
Lead a peer refinement session — analyse a group member's performance, provide structured feedback, support the refinement attempt, and evaluate the outcome

response_modes.reason: Adapting and refining movement skills builds through practice across multiple activity contexts and feedback cycles. A single adaptation attempt is insufficient — students need to develop a repertoire of adaptive responses across different movement challenges, equipment types, and performance contexts. The elaborations explicitly require multiple activity types.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Digital feedback cycles, novel activity transfer, and peer refinement leadership each add a genuinely different adaptive context. Students who engage the wider tier develop adaptive capability that is not dependent on a single activity type — they can analyse, adapt and refine across unfamiliar movement challenges.
success_criteria: Makes a specific adaptation in response to analysis or feedback
Evaluates whether the adaptation improved the performance outcome with reference to observable evidence
Adaptation is connected to the analysis — not a random change
